root_cause: The 'NPU Models Tests / 6010' job's TensorFlow model-hub step downloads pretrained Keras application weights (ResNet50) from storage.googleapis.com at test time. On this Windows runner, the Winsock DNS resolver call getaddrinfo failed for that hostname (error 11001, WSAHOST_NOT_FOUND), so the HTTP download used by keras.utils.file_utils.get_file could not even establish a connection. This is a transient DNS/network resolution problem on the runner's network path to storage.googleapis.com (outside the OpenVINO plugin/test code, and unrelated to PR #38948's actual change, which only de-duplicated two PyTorch layer test method names). All other TensorFlow, PyTorch, JAX, and NPU conversion tests in the same job passed, including other Kaggle/HuggingFace downloads that succeeded moments earlier, which further points to an isolated resolver hiccup for this specific external host rather than a systemic outage.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside CI since it depends on transient DNS resolution of storage.googleapis.com from the Windows runner's network. To approximate locally: run `python -m pytest install/tests/model_hub_tests/tensorflow/test_tf_convert_model.py -k ResNet50 -m precommit --ie_device NPU` on a Windows host configured like the CI runner, optionally while simulating DNS failures for storage.googleapis.com (e.g., via a hosts-file block or firewall rule) to confirm the same getaddrinfo failure path.
recommended_actions: No code fix required for PR #38948; the failure is unrelated to its changes (test method de-duplication in PyTorch layer tests).
Re-run the 'NPU Models Tests / 6010' job; this class of DNS failure is typically transient and resolves on retry.

If this host (storage.googleapis.com) continues to fail intermittently, consider caching/mirroring the Keras ResNet50 weights artifact internally (similar to other model caches already used in the hub tests) to reduce dependency on live external DNS/network availability during CI.

Monitor the pattern database entry 30a2eda292a88eb7 for recurrence; if it starts occurring frequently, escalate to the CI infrastructure team to investigate DNS reliability for storage.googleapis.com from the Windows runner pool.
prevention_strategies: Reduce hard dependency on live third-party DNS/network availability during precommit CI by pre-caching or mirroring frequently-used model weight downloads (e.g., Keras application weights) in an internal artifact store, and add retry-with-backoff around keras.utils.file_utils.get_file-based downloads in the model-hub test harness so a single transient DNS blip does not fail the whole job.
historical_context: Several past Network-category patterns exist for this repository's post-commit runs, including DNS resolution failures during git checkout ('Could not resolve host: github.com', pattern eeae3ce3f5218e80), getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN during artifact upload (pattern d877f2bb57b833d0, count 2), and HuggingFace 429 rate limiting during model downloads (pattern 4dd69b5f0be10a15). This is the first recorded occurrence of a DNS/getaddrinfo failure specifically for storage.googleapis.com while downloading Keras application weights, so a new pattern entry (30a2eda292a88eb7) was created.
